name: Apache Derby
tagline: Pure-Java embedded SQL database from the Cloudscape lineage, retired by Apache in 2025.
description: Apache Derby is a standards-oriented relational database written entirely in Java, descended from Cloudscape and donated by IBM to Apache in 2004. It runs embedded in a JVM or as a network server, and for years shipped with the JDK as Java DB, making it a common choice for tests, tooling and small embedded apps. On 2025-10-10 the Derby developers voted to retire the project into a read-only state: development and bug fixing ended and no further releases will be published, so 10.17.1.0 from 2023 is the final version. Existing users should plan a move to H2, HSQLDB or SQLite for embedding, or PostgreSQL for server use.
statusNote: Retired by its PMC on 2025-10-10; read-only, no further releases or fixes. Final release 10.17.1.0. Migrate to H2, HSQLDB or PostgreSQL.

scale.notes: Single JVM or single network server; asynchronous replication for one standby.

strengths: Pure Java with a small footprint; embeds with a single JAR
Strict SQL standard conformance and JDBC compliance
Same database usable embedded or via the network server
Built-in disk encryption and Java stored procedures
weaknesses: Project retired: no security fixes or new releases
Slower than H2 or HSQLDB for most embedded workloads
No JSON, full-text search or modern SQL features
useCases: Maintaining legacy Java applications that already embed Derby
Read-only reference for existing test suites
